newsitem.title: DENMARK: Panel confirms Lauritzen Danyard price.
newsitem.headline: Panel confirms Lauritzen Danyard price.

text.p: Danish shipping and shipbuilding group J. Lauritzen said on Friday an independent panel had confirmed the $100 million sale price of its Danyard shipyard unit to Penang Shipbuilding Construction (PSC).
On April 1, Lauritzen finalised the sale of a 48 percent stake in Danyard to PSC, with the deal subject to the approval of the Malaysian authorities.
PSC at that time paid a one million dollar deposit but delays set in.
Lauritzen had expected the $100 million deal to be approved in July, whereupon PSC would pay a further $nine million and payment would be completed this month.

According to a letter of intent signed last December, the final purchase sum could be revised depending on the result of an independent evaluation of Danyard by British consultants Jones Lang & Wootton.
"After several months' delay, the evaluation has been received and studied by PSC and the originally agreed purchase sum of $100 million remains unchanged," Lauritzen said in a statement.

Lauritzen said its application for approval of the deal would now be sent to the Malaysian authorities next week and a final closing would take place after PSC shareholders had approved it. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
